editorial:
Imagine a guy who thinks he is the hottest thing on the planet just because he is a famous TV star. That is Robert, a vain man who spends his days tricking young women into falling for him, only to dump them once he gets bored. He thinks he has every move figured out until he meets Marion. She is a nineteen-year-old American who is totally different from the girls he usually dates. She is honest, blunt, and refuses to play into his romantic games. The vibe is light, breezy, and full of funny clashes between a man who loves himself too much and a girl who sees right through him.

You will love the chemistry between the leads and how the movie pokes fun at celebrity egos. The pacing is quick and the dialogue feels natural, though some of the jokes might feel a bit dated since it is from 1970. If you enjoy witty rom-coms where a smug guy gets humbled, you should definitely give this a shot. You can find it by renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you love physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is a great way to keep this gem.
endingExplained: After a lot of back-and-forth and ego battles, Robert finally realizes that Marion is the only person who actually challenges him and keeps him honest. He stops playing the field and decides he truly wants to be with her. The movie wraps up with Robert abandoning his vain ways for a real relationship. He learns that honesty is better than a fake persona, and the two end up together in a happy, unexpected partnership.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romantic comedies and seeing arrogant characters get their comeuppance.
